updates.title: TBRLucas Security & Reliability Review
updates.summary: Routine security and reliability review completed. Two low-severity issues were corrected; no Critical, High or Medium findings were identified in the reviewed scope.
updates.details:
## Review scope
Reviewed the public-site source, page scripts, content publishing and administration flow, image upload handling, Worker authentication/session/CORS design, public JSON data, and recent GitHub Pages deployment records. The live pages could not be independently fetched through the available page checker, so deployment verification is based on GitHub Actions.

## Findings and corrections

### Low — image upload file extensions
The blog cover uploader previously derived the stored file extension from the original filename, even though it separately checked the image MIME type. It now chooses the extension from the accepted image type (JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF). This prevents misleading filename extensions from determining how uploaded files are served.

### Low — duplicated status entry
The Status page showed both the main site and Backupsite, although both checks targeted the same main-site address and maintenance settings. It now reports only the main website, avoiding a duplicated and misleading status.

## Remaining hardening note
The authenticated administration upload flow still has a credential-handling design that would benefit from moving the upload operation fully server-side. No change was made because that requires a Cloudflare Worker deployment and end-to-end testing. The current review did not identify evidence of credential exposure to unauthenticated visitors.

## Result
No Critical, High or Medium findings were identified in the files reviewed. This was a focused maintenance review, not a comprehensive penetration test or a guarantee of security.

updates.title: Blog Themes Expanded with Default Theme Support
updates.summary: The blog now includes a default theme based on the website's original design, alongside the three special article themes: iOS 6, Android Market (2012), and Dark 2010s.
updates.details:
- Added the Default theme to the article design selector.
- New blog posts use the Default theme automatically.
- Older posts without a selected design also keep the original website styling.
- The iOS 6, Android Market (2012), and Dark 2010s themes remain available.
- Themes only affect individual blog articles and do not change the rest of the website.

updates.title: A Major Update: The New TBRLucas Website
updates.summary: The main TBRLucas website has received a major update, bringing together the improvements developed on Backupsite and introducing a refreshed experience.
updates.details:
## The TBRLucas Website Is Finally Complete!

Well, this is a big one.

After a lot of work, changes, experiments and redesigns, the development of the TBRLucas website has finally come to an end.

We've brought everything we worked on over the past updates together, including the improvements that were previously made on Backupsite. Here's a look at what's new.

### Blog

The blog received quite a few improvements. You can now find cover images on posts, pictures inside articles and clickable links. The editor was also improved with image uploading and better formatting tools.

We also worked on the search feature, featured articles and navigation between posts.

And, of course, there are now several different article designs: Default, iOS 6, Android Market (2012), Dark 2010s, Aero and Cydia Classic.

### Downloads

The Downloads section got a refresh, including its main page and individual download pages. Everything is now better organized and ready for new additions.

### The rest of the website

We also made changes to the Home, Projects, About, Blog, Status and 404 pages.

The What's New page received improvements too, and now there's a section on the homepage where you can see the latest updates without having to look for them.

### A little more personality

We added two seasonal themes: Happy XMAS, available from December 1 to December 26, and Happy New Year, from December 27 to January 2.

There are also four custom SVG favicons: the regular TBRLucas icon, a GTA VI-inspired version, a Christmas version and a New Year version. They change automatically along with the seasonal themes.

### So, what's next?

This is where the website's development officially ends.

From now on, we won't be planning major redesigns or adding new features. Our focus will be on keeping the website secure and publishing new content.

The only updates you should expect are security improvements, new posts on the Blog and new additions to Downloads.

### And one last thing...

A big thank you to all the websites we used as references during development. Their designs and ideas helped us along the way.

Special thanks to Apple, Google, YouTube, Microsoft, Samsung, Internet Archive and Web Design Museum.

And, of course, thank YOU for taking the time to read this page and check out the website.

Whether you've been following the project for a while or just discovered it today, we really appreciate it.

That's all for the development updates. Now it's time to focus on what comes next!

**Thanks for being here.**

TBRLucas
